source_snapshot.procedure: Enable Platform First Error Handling, MCA threshold enable/count FFE and Reset After Sync-Flood; unlock CPU through HDT; boot Ubuntu 20.04, RHEL 9.0 or Windows 2022; install AMD RAS tool; list links; then inject error type 1 at hardcoded link 0 for IOD location 0 and CCD location 1. Step labels incorrectly call both injections Correctable.
source_snapshot.criteria: For uncorrectable errors the tool reports PASS and the OS reports within an unspecified timeout; inspect dmesg and the injection report against an unspecified AMD RAS specification.

source_snapshot.procedure_direct_xlsx: 【Before Test】 1. Check that the SUT configuration (e.g., hardware, firmware, drivers, etc.) matches the specifications/recipe definition. 2. Clear logs (e.g., dmesg, syslog, SEL, etc.). 【During Test】 Hardware required: RDIMM with ECC / HDT Software tool: AMD RAS Error Injection Tool 1. BIOS settings: a. CPU Common Options → Platform First Error Handling: Enabled b. CPU Common Options → MCA error thresh enable: TRUE c. CPU Common Options → MCA error thresh count: FFE (Deviate from default setting FF5) d. FCH Common Options → FCH RAS Options → Reset After Sync-Flood: Enable 2. Unlock CPU via HDT. 3. Boot into Ubuntu 20.04/RHEL 9.0 / Windows 2022. 4. Download the AMD RAS Error Injection Tool, then install and open the software. 5. Enter the following commands: sudo ./cmdline_amdraserrorinjectiontest --listgmilinks 6. Run IOD Correctable Error Injection sudo ./cmdline_amdraserrorinjectiontest --gmixgmi --linknumber 0 --errorlocation 0 --linktraffic 1 --errortype 1 7. Run CCD Correctable Error Injection sudo ./cmdline_amdraserrorinjectiontest --gmixgmi --linknumber 0 --errorlocation 1 --linktraffic 1 --errortype 1 【After Test】 1. Collect test results and photos, and save them to specific folders. 2. Check if there are unexpected logs (e.g., dmesg, syslog, SEL, etc.) generate after test.
source_snapshot.criteria_direct_xlsx: 1. For Uncorrectable errors, the tool provides a PASS status. 2. If the OS reports the error within a timeout period, the test passed. 3. If the OS does not report the error within a timeout period, the test failed. 4. Follow the AMD RAS Spec to check the dmesg and Error inject report.
source_snapshot.deepseek_direct_xlsx: PARTIAL | -- GMI3 Uncorrectable Error: inject the GMI3 GMI3 Uncorrectable Error via the AMD RAS Error Injection Tool (after HDT/unlock + the BIOS RAS knobs from the procedure, e.g. Platform First Error Handling=Enabled + per-unit MCA/UMC settings). Agent stages/verifies with sshpass -p "$DUT_PASS" ssh -o StrictHostKeyChecking=no $DUT_USER@$DUT_IP "dmesg -T 2>&1 | tail -160 | grep -iE 'gmi|xgmi|link.error|corrected|uncorrected'; echo __GMI3_GMI3_Uncorrectable_Error; ipmitool sel elist 2>&1 | tail -40 2>&1" but the tool injection step itself is interactive/HW-level and needs the user to drive the exact inject command.

disposition_reason: In fault injection, a copied Correctable label is safety-critical because the numeric errortype selects behavior that may reset or crash the fabric. Tool PASS can mean the request was accepted even when the DUT response is wrong. Therefore the physical link, error severity, expected containment and recovery deadline must be decided before one injection. The second location cannot follow automatically after a disruptive first event, and Windows requires WHEA/console evidence rather than dmesg. These are resolvable execution prerequisites, not a reason to discard the case.
